text:
maria: Seeing gaps in traces for jobs that go gateway -> kafka -> worker. Spans start in gateway but not linked in worker. Anyone else seeing this?
kevin: Yep saw this in staging, reproduced it. Looks like some kafka headers are getting truncated or mangled.
alex: What propagation format are we using right now? W3C traceparent + tracestate, or a custom blob?
maria: W3C traceparent + tracestate. We also add a small baggage JSON in x-otel-baggage and a base64 blob in x-otel-context for older workers. Workers rely on OTEL auto-instrumentation to pick it up.
jess: For kafka we were stuffing a json blob into a header (x-otel-context) and encoding as base64. Kafka headers are binary but some client serializers seem to drop NULs or truncate if header size gets large.
samir: Related: SQS had attribute size limits. For Kafka, broker and client configs (max.message.bytes, header.max.size?) matter. Also compression can change how headers survive the roundtrip.
kevin: I logged the consumer record in staging — header value was cut off mid-base64. OTEL SDK failed to parse -> worker started a new root span, so trace link broken.
ops-oncall: Prod impact: request id 7f3a9b... we see ~3% of async tasks unlinking from parent traces over last 24h, correlated with spikes in payload size. Infra was paged earlier.
alex: Proposal: switch to minimal W3C traceparent only in headers (keep tracestate tiny) and write a compact backup into the message payload (e.g., hex-encoded trace + span + sampled flag). Payload backup avoids header length fragility.
jess: Changing format is risky for older workers. Backward compat: gateway can dual-write (header W3C + payload field trace_ctx) so old workers still work. Also we should show in Console a badge like "linked via payload" so SREs know it's fallback.
maria: Also need to ensure sampling decision survives. We had cases where tracestate got stripped; per-tenant sampling should be explicit.
samir: We already annotate tracestate with rd=s:1 but some libs strip tracestate. Maybe add a tiny header x-rd-sampled: 1/0 as redundancy.
kevin: Quick mitigation: I'll add logic in gateway to, when header parse fails on consumer side, emit a metric trace.header_truncations and attach a link to the raw record for debugging. Will open PR.
dev-bot: deploy-bot: canary-gateway v2.3.1 deployed to staging at 1799943330 :rocket:
jess: Long-term: consider sidecar collector that ingest OTLP from gateway/worker and uses an explicit correlation id in the Kafka payload. But that increases OTLP traffic and retention costs.
ops-oncall: Important retention note: our collector drops attributes larger than 64KB and truncates long string attributes. If we embed full JSON context in payload we may hit retention/ingest rejections. Compactness matters.
maria: I'll draft an RFC: dual-write approach (W3C header + compact payload trace hex), add x-rd-sampled boolean header, and Console UX to surface fallback links. Will include rollout plan to maintain backwards compat.
kevin: Thanks — I'll open the gateway PR with unit tests for header length, base64 truncation, and consumer fallback parsing.
alex: Tiny example for the payload approach: 
```
traceparent: 00-4bf92f3577b34da6a3ce929d0e0e4736-00f067aa0ba902b7-01
// payload.trace_ctx = "4bf92f3577b34da6a3ce929d0e0e4736:00f067aa0ba902b7:1"
// gateway: headers.put("traceparent","00-..." ); payload.put("trace_ctx", hex);
```
jess: Also add an integration test that runs with a broker configured to simulate header truncation. We should catch this in CI.
ops-oncall: Agreed. Ping me on the RFC when ready and I'll run a focused prod sweep after canary.
maria: Will do. Thanks all.
